title: Why Stomping Your Brakes Used to Cause Crashes

scenes.narration: Why does stomping your brakes at full force make a car skid harder, until ABS intervenes?
scenes.objective: Hook: wheel locks up, then ABS saves it

scenes.narration: When you slam the brakes, your tires don't stop you faster by locking up. They completely lose control.
scenes.objective: Show locked wheel sliding vs rolling with grip

scenes.narration: Static friction where rubber grips pavement is thirty percent stronger than kinetic friction when a locked tire skids.
scenes.objective: Visualize static vs kinetic friction at contact patch

scenes.narration: Magnetic wheel speed sensors detect a tire locking up in milliseconds.
scenes.objective: Hall-effect sensor reads tone ring teeth passing

scenes.narration: The ABS hydraulic modulator pulses brake fluid pressure up to twenty times per second, rapidly releasing and reapplying the brake pad.
scenes.objective: Modulator valves cycle: inlet closes, outlet opens, pump runs

scenes.narration: This keeps the tire at the threshold of maximum static friction, letting you steer around obstacles while stopping in the shortest distance.
scenes.objective: System working together: sensor -> modulator -> caliper -> tire grip

scenes.narration: The rapid shutter in your pedal isn't a malfunction; it's physics saving your life.
scenes.objective: Exploded view of full ABS brake system collapsing into place
